handbookNote: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide, July 2025 edition (document code 'DSD CDL 10.30'), published by the Illinois Secretary of State -- the official PDF is served from ilsos.gov/content/dam/publications/pdf_publications/dsd_cdl10.pdf, but that domain sits behind an Akamai WAF that stalled every direct fetch attempt (curl, PowerShell WebClient, and a live Chrome browser session all hung indefinitely against it in this environment); the identical official file was instead retrieved via its web.archive.org mirror (snapshot timestamp 2026-01-07, confirmed HTTP 200) on 2026-08-21/22 and converted to plain text via pdftotext (scratchpad/il_cdl_research/il_cdl_manual.txt, 9,733 lines) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: the Illinois guide's own Section 1.4.1 ('Computerized Written Knowledge Testing') states exact question counts for every Illinois CDL knowledge test -- General (core) Knowledge: 30 standardized multiple-choice questions, 80% minimum passing score (24 correct); Combination endorsement: 20 questions; Air Brakes: 25 questions; Passenger (P): 20 questions; Tank Vehicle (N): 20 questions; School Bus (S): 20 questions (same test also satisfies the Illinois School Bus Permit (SBP) requirement); Hazardous Materials (H): 30 questions (TSA background check/approval required first); Doubles/Triples (T): 20 questions; Charter Bus (C): 20 questions -- every test computes to exactly the federally standardized 80% minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a). Notably Illinois's own general-knowledge item count (30) is smaller than several other states already built in this project (e.g. Idaho's 50) -- confirmed directly from Illinois's own manual, not assumed from precedent. The same Section 1.3.6 confirms Illinois's CDL/CLP fee structure (CDL renewal/out-of-state transfer age 18-69: $60 total = $10 base DL + $24 CDL + $6 CDLIS + $20 Motor Carrier Safety Inspection Fund; CLP: $50; upgrade/add/remove class or endorsement: $5) and CLP-to-CDL rules (a CLP issued to upgrade class, remove the air-brakes restriction, or add a Passenger/School Bus endorsement must be held at least 14 days before skills/drive testing). Content-depth rationale: Illinois runs its own state-authored CDL Guide (not a generic AAMVA model manual) with several state-specific features not present in most other states built so far in this project -- a distinct Class D non-CDL category, a seventh endorsement letter (X = Combined Hazardous Materials & Tank Vehicle) alongside the standard P/N/S/H/T, and a wholly Illinois-specific Charter Bus (C) endorsement/Section 11 for buses transporting school children on district charter trips. It covers Section 1 Introduction (CMV definition, CDL/CLP classifications and endorsements, type restrictions, standards/requirements, medical certification, testing structure, disqualifications, electronic devices, vehicle size/lighting/registration, IRP/IFTA), Section 2 Driving Safely (vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing, communicating, speed/space management, hazard perception, distracted/aggressive driving, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, emergencies, ABS, skids, accidents, fires, alcohol/drugs, fatigue, hazmat-for-all-drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (communication rules/shipping papers/placarding plus loading/driving/emergency rules), Section 10 School Bus, Section 11 Charter Bus, Section 12 Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 13 Basic Control Skills Test, Section 14 On-Road Driving Test, and Section 15 Special CDL/CLP Information & Programs (CLP rules, National-Registry medical certification, military written-test exemption, Illinois Fast Pass scheduling, third-party testing, ELDT, drug/alcohol clearinghouse) -- supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question pool. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Illinois manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
